summary: A full audit of the .claude agent surface found systematic citation drift in the ungoverned corpus; the skills-check validator now enforces citation integrity, and this record fixes the recurrence mechanism so the surface cannot silently rot again.
observation: Before 2026-08-10 no component owned .claude: impact analysis returned unassigned with no validators, and the corpus had drifted exactly as unowned knowledge does. The audit found 8 stale citations (docs/rag.md cited twice but never written, services/billing/ and services/channels/ cited as reference implementations but never generated, email_tasks.py and cleanup_tasks.py cited as examples but absent), one auto-loaded rule file teaching the wrong test harness (pytest-asyncio with real-session fixtures against an anyio mocked-session conftest), and a facade rule stated as fact that the rag package has never satisfied. Every drifted file was template-era; every governance-era file was clean - authorship inside the envelope correlated exactly with accuracy.

evidence.detail: 8 findings across 22 files on first run; 0 findings after the S2-S4 content sessions; strict mode and the CI step landed in the ratchet session with the corpus already clean.
Before: unassigned, no validators. After: agent-operating-surface, validators skills-check + governance-check.

prod-debug validated end to end against live telemetry: 11,695 records/24h from service fullstack (development), and the exception-triage query surfaced 13 auth-domain exceptions generated minutes earlier by the Playwright auth specs - the two validation streams observed each other. e2e-playwright harness validated: 166 tests across 5 browser projects in 1.9m via make playwright with working auth.setup storage state; the suite itself is red (128 passed, 33 failed, 5 not run, stable across a frontend image rebuild) with two real findings - integrations.spec content drift (page renders, Gmail card copy 'identify the connected mailbox' absent) on all browsers, and a webkit/Mobile Safari cluster on chat specs. template-upgrade front half validated: upgrade-dry-run ran against a real pending upstream release (migration 0027 users.magic_link_epoch, enforced auth rate limits, COOKIE_SECURE, two removed env vars) after exposing that the upstream tool crashes on a Windows cp1252 console without PYTHONUTF8=1. Apply/finalize remains deferred to a real upgrade decision; the e2e failures are follow-up fix-issue work, not harness defects.

proposed_action: Three-layer recurrence mechanism: (1) skills-check runs strict in CI and via impact selection on every .claude-touching session; (2) debt-sweep's survey now includes the agent surface - gate-metrics verdict trends and a prose-accuracy spot-check of one skill per sweep, because skills-check proves citations exist, not that descriptions are true; (3) a template upgrade re-runs skills-check over any upstream .claude changes before finalize (template-upgrade skill, rule 4). Repeat a full manual audit when a batch of new skills lands or a template upgrade rewrites the surface.
